summary: The safety component is the verify/gate stage of the loop. Before any ToolCall leaves the reason stage and reaches the act stage, SafetyChecker validates the command/URL/path, PathValidator confirms the target stays inside the working sandbox, PermissionStore decides whether a matching PermissionGrant lets it skip confirmation, SecretScanner and VulnerabilityDetector scan payloads for leaked credentials and dangerous patterns, and AuditLogger records every decision as an AuditEvent. It is a hard gate: it can block, redact, or wave through a ToolCall, reshaping loop control at the boundary between deciding and doing.
context_basis: Recommendations were formed reading src/safety/ (checker, path_validator, permissions, audit, scanner, tool_metadata) in the context of the full engine at a ~600k budget framing, where safety sits inline in execute_single_tool as the last gate before a tool runs.

examples.title: Gate every ToolCall before it acts
examples.intent: Ensure no ToolCall reaches the act stage without passing SafetyChecker validation.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Inserts a mandatory verify node between reason and act; a failed SafetyCheck short-circuits the iteration back to reason instead of executing.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Draw an edge from the reasoner node into the safety gate node so every emitted ToolCall is routed through it.
touch_interaction.visual: The gate node renders as a hexagon with a shield glyph; the inbound edge pulses amber while a check is in flight and turns green on pass, red on block.

examples.mini_scenario: The reasoner emits a shell ToolCall to run rm -rf; SafetyChecker flags it, the gate raises a SafetyBlock, and the loop returns to reason for an alternative.
examples.pitfall: Do not let any tool path bypass the gate; a single un-gated edge defeats the whole verify stage.

examples.title: Confine writes with PathValidator
examples.intent: Prevent file ToolCalls from escaping the working directory sandbox.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Adds a per-path validation before act; a path outside the allowed list transitions the loop to ErrorRecovery rather than mutating the filesystem.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the safety node to open a radial menu and pin the sandbox root path used by PathValidator.
touch_interaction.visual: A dotted boundary ring animates around the node; paths inside pulse blue, escaping paths flash a red slash badge.

examples.mini_scenario: A write ToolCall targets ../../etc/hosts; PathValidator's lexical normalization catches the traversal and blocks it before any disk mutation.
examples.pitfall: Validate the lexically-normalized path and symlink target, not the raw string, or a ../ or symlink escapes the sandbox.

examples.title: Skip confirmation with a PermissionGrant
examples.intent: Let trusted, pre-authorized ToolCalls run without pausing the loop for user confirmation.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: When PermissionStore.is_authorized matches, the control loop skips the human-in-the-loop pause and stays in continuous execution.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the permissions sub-node to view active grants; each grant chip shows its tool_pattern and expiry.
touch_interaction.visual: Matched grants render as green key badges; the fast-path edge glows steady green while confirmation edges dim.

examples.mini_scenario: A session grant for read_file matches an incoming read ToolCall, so is_authorized returns true and the loop executes it without a prompt.
examples.pitfall: Scope grants tightly with with_resource; an over-broad tool_pattern silently waves through unintended ToolCalls.

examples.title: Expire temporary grants on the timeline
examples.intent: Auto-revoke a permission after a duration so the fast path narrows over the loop's lifetime.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: PermissionGrant.is_expired flips a previously-authorized ToolCall back to requiring confirmation, re-inserting the human pause into control.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch the permission chip to inspect its countdown; the chip shrinks as time-to-expiry decreases.
touch_interaction.visual: Temporary grants render with a draining ring timer; on expiry they gray out and drop from the active set.

examples.mini_scenario: A temporary run_shell grant expires mid-session; the next shell ToolCall no longer matches and the loop re-prompts the user.
examples.pitfall: Do not treat is_authorized as permanent; re-check on every ToolCall since temporary grants expire between iterations.

examples.title: Scan payloads for leaked secrets
examples.intent: Block ToolCalls whose content leaks API keys or credentials via SecretScanner.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Adds a scan_content pass over tool output/args; a high-severity SecurityFinding halts the act and routes to redaction or block.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap the scanner sub-node to expand a list of matched SecretPatterns and their severities.
touch_interaction.visual: Findings stack as severity-colored bars (critical red, high orange); the node pulses when a scan is active.

examples.mini_scenario: A commit ToolCall's diff contains an AWS key; SecretScanner emits a critical SecurityFinding and the gate blocks the push.
examples.pitfall: Scan both inbound args and outbound results; secrets can leak in tool output that gets fed back to the model.

examples.title: Detect dangerous code patterns
examples.intent: Flag injection-prone or unsafe patterns before generated code is written or executed.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: VulnerabilityDetector.scan_content annotates a ToolCall with SecurityFindings that can downgrade RiskLevel handling or block the act.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread on the scanner node to zoom into per-finding detail: title, CWE, remediation, snippet.
touch_interaction.visual: Each finding renders a CWE tag chip; the node border thickens with the count of unresolved findings.

examples.mini_scenario: A code-write ToolCall introduces a shell-injection sink; the detector attaches a high SecurityFinding with a CWE and remediation note.
examples.pitfall: Findings are advisory unless wired to block; decide per RiskLevel whether a finding gates or merely annotates.

examples.title: Classify tool risk to pick a mode
examples.intent: Route each ToolCall to confirm, auto, or block based on its classified RiskLevel.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: classify_tool_metadata assigns a RiskLevel that the control loop maps to ExecutionMode, deciding whether to pause.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap a tool node to see its RiskLevel badge (Safe/Low/Medium/High) and the mode it triggers.
touch_interaction.visual: Nodes are tinted by risk: green Safe, yellow Medium, red High; higher risk pulses faster.

examples.mini_scenario: A network fetch is classified Medium; normal_mode_needs_confirmation returns true and the loop pauses for approval.
examples.pitfall: Keep tool_metadata classifications current; an unclassified tool defaults conservatively and may over-prompt or under-guard.

examples.title: Log every decision as an AuditEvent
examples.intent: Persist a durable JSONL trail of tool executions and safety blocks for replay and forensics.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: AuditLogger writes an AuditEvent on every tool execution and block, giving the loop an observable, replayable history without altering control flow.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick up on the audit node to scroll the append-only event stream in a side panel.
touch_interaction.visual: A ticking log ribbon streams entries; ToolExecution rows are gray, SafetyBlock rows are red-tagged.

examples.mini_scenario: log_safety_block records a blocked destructive command; the AuditEvent lands in the session JSONL for later review.
examples.pitfall: Never mutate past AuditEvents; the log is append-only and its integrity is the basis for post-hoc trust.

examples.title: Pin DNS to block SSRF rebinding
examples.intent: Prevent tool HTTP calls from reaching private/internal addresses via DNS rebinding.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: PinnedDnsResolver plus is_private_or_internal reject internal targets before the act stage opens a socket.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the network guard to toggle allow_localhost / allow_file_scheme flags.
touch_interaction.visual: The guard renders a globe with a firewall ring; private-IP resolutions flash a red block badge.

examples.mini_scenario: A fetch ToolCall resolves a hostname to 169.254.169.254; is_private_or_internal returns true and the gate blocks the metadata-endpoint access.
examples.pitfall: Resolve and pin the IP once, then connect to the pinned IP; re-resolving invites a rebind between check and connect.

examples.title: Redact sensitive output before feedback
examples.intent: Strip secrets from tool output before it is fed back into the model's context.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The redact pass rewrites tool result content, keeping the perceive-back edge clean so secrets never enter the reasoning context.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Draw an edge from the tool-output port through the redact node before it loops back to the reasoner.
touch_interaction.visual: Redacted spans render as black bars in the output preview; the node shows a masking icon.

examples.mini_scenario: A log-reading ToolCall surfaces a bearer token; redact replaces it with [REDACTED] before the output re-enters context.
examples.pitfall: Redact before the output is appended to Messages, not after; once in context the secret is already exposed to the model.

examples.title: Dry-run high-risk acts first
examples.intent: Preview the effect of a destructive ToolCall without executing it.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: In dry_run ExecutionMode the act stage produces a simulated result, letting the loop verify intent before a real mutation.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap the gate to toggle dry-run mode; queued acts show a ghost preview instead of running.
touch_interaction.visual: Nodes in dry-run render translucent with a dashed 'SIM' badge; no side-effect glow fires.

examples.mini_scenario: A migration ToolCall runs in dry-run first, printing the intended schema change so the user confirms before the real apply.
examples.pitfall: Ensure the tool actually honors dry-run; a tool that ignores the mode will mutate state despite the ghost preview.

examples.title: YOLO mode: measured gate removal
examples.intent: Allow an operator to intentionally disable confirmation for a trusted autonomous run.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: yolo mode sets ExecutionMode to auto-approve, collapsing the verify pause so the loop runs uninterrupted.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Rotate the mode dial on the gate node from Guarded to YOLO; a confirmation overlay warns before committing.
touch_interaction.visual: The whole gate node turns high-contrast orange with a lightning badge to signal guards are relaxed.

examples.mini_scenario: An operator flips YOLO for a sandboxed batch job; tool executions proceed without prompts but every call is still audited.
examples.pitfall: YOLO removes confirmation, not auditing or path validation; never let it also disable the sandbox or the log.

examples.title: Score findings to prioritize the gate
examples.intent: Use SecuritySeverity.score to decide which findings block versus warn.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Aggregated finding scores feed a threshold that the verify stage uses to branch between block, warn, and pass.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spread to fan out findings sorted by score; drag a threshold slider to set the block cutoff.
touch_interaction.visual: Findings arrange on a heat gradient; those above the slider glow red as blockers.

examples.mini_scenario: Two low findings and one critical arrive; the summed score crosses the block threshold and the gate stops the act.
examples.pitfall: Blocking on raw count invites noise; weight by severity score so many low findings do not outweigh one critical.

examples.title: Sanitize the process environment
examples.intent: Strip sensitive env vars before a shell ToolCall spawns a child process.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: process_env filters the environment handed to the act stage's child, preventing credential inheritance across the loop boundary.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press the shell node to edit the env allowlist/denylist applied at spawn.
touch_interaction.visual: Denied vars render as struck-through chips; the node shows a filter funnel icon.

examples.mini_scenario: A shell ToolCall would inherit CLOUD_API_KEY; process_env scrubs it so the child cannot read the credential.
examples.pitfall: Scrub at spawn time for each ToolCall; caching a scrubbed env can leak vars added later in the session.

examples.title: Split and check compound shell commands
examples.intent: Validate each sub-command of a chained shell command independently.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: split_shell_commands and normalize_shell_command let the gate evaluate every segment, blocking the whole ToolCall if any part is unsafe.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tap a shell node to expand its && / ; / | segments as a chain of mini gate chips.
touch_interaction.visual: Each segment chip lights green or red; one red chip turns the parent node red.

examples.mini_scenario: A command git pull && rm -rf build is split; the first segment passes but the second is flagged, blocking the whole call.
examples.pitfall: Check every segment; a benign prefix must not launder a dangerous suffix through the gate.

examples.title: Detect vulnerable dependencies
examples.intent: Flag a ToolCall that adds or uses a known-vulnerable dependency.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Dependency.is_vulnerable produces a SecurityFinding that the verify stage can surface before a build or install act proceeds.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap the dependency node to list packages with a vulnerability badge and version.
touch_interaction.visual: Vulnerable deps render with a red bug badge and CWE tag; clean deps are muted.

examples.mini_scenario: An add-dependency ToolCall pins a package version flagged by is_vulnerable; the gate warns before the install act.
examples.pitfall: Match on name and version; a fixed patch release of the same package must not inherit the older advisory.

examples.title: Return a structured PermissionResult
examples.intent: Make the authorization outcome an inspectable object rather than a bare boolean.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: PermissionResult carries the decision plus reason, so the control loop can render why a ToolCall was allowed, denied, or needs confirmation.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tap a pending ToolCall to reveal its PermissionResult card with allow/deny reason.
touch_interaction.visual: Allowed cards are green, denied red, needs-confirm amber, each showing the matched grant or missing reason.

examples.mini_scenario: A ToolCall with no matching grant returns a needs-confirm PermissionResult; the UI shows the reason and asks the user.
examples.pitfall: Surface the reason to the user; a bare deny with no explanation makes the loop feel arbitrary and erodes trust.

examples.title: Check symlink safety on file targets
examples.intent: Follow symlinks and confirm the real target stays inside the sandbox.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: PathValidator.check_symlink_safety resolves links before the act stage writes, blocking a symlink that points outside the allowed tree.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-press a file node to trace its symlink chain rendered as a hop path.
touch_interaction.visual: Symlink hops draw as dashed arrows; a hop that leaves the boundary ring flashes red.

examples.mini_scenario: A write targets logs/latest which symlinks to /etc; check_symlink_safety resolves it and blocks the escaping write.
examples.pitfall: Validate the resolved target, not the link path; a link inside the sandbox can still point outside it.

examples.title: Bracket the run with session audit markers
examples.intent: Emit session-start and session-end AuditEvents that bound the run's audit trail.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: log_session_start and log_session_end frame the whole loop lifecycle, giving replay tools clean boundaries for the run.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flick down on the audit node to jump to the session-start marker; flick up for session-end.
touch_interaction.visual: Start and end markers render as bold bookend bars anchoring the event ribbon.

examples.mini_scenario: The agent boots, log_session_start writes an opening AuditEvent, and on Stop log_session_end closes the trail with a matching id.
examples.pitfall: Always emit the end marker, even on failure paths, or partial audit trails complicate forensic replay.

examples.title: Compose the full gate as one verify node
examples.intent: Fuse checker, path validation, permissions, scanning, and audit into a single ordered gate.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Chains SafetyCheck -> PathValidator -> PermissionStore -> SecretScanner -> AuditLogger so one verify node decides pass/block for every ToolCall.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinch to collapse the five safety sub-nodes into one compact gate chip, or spread to expand the pipeline.
touch_interaction.visual: Collapsed it shows a shield with a stage-count badge; expanded it reveals the ordered sub-node pipeline with per-stage status lights.

examples.mini_scenario: One shell ToolCall flows through all five sub-checks in order; permissions pass but the scanner flags a secret, so the aggregate gate blocks and audits.
examples.pitfall: Preserve the ordering: validate and authorize before scanning content, and always audit last regardless of outcome.
